quotes.text: I have long believed in the need to prepare our electric grid for the realities of increasing energy demand brought on by onshoring of manufacturing, AI and data centers, and the electrification of our economy, spurred on by the IRA, while also securing our clean energy future.

Congratulations to Arnav from Fremd High School for winning this year's Congressional App Challenge! Arnav developed his app, Oculare AI, to address the accessibility crisis in eye disease screening. Millions of people lack access to ophthalmologists and diagnostic equipment. 

All submissions were judged by students from Harper College. Thank you for taking the time to encourage students in coding!

AI could bring enormous benefits, from medical research and drug development to practical fixes like addressing bus bunching. It also carries real risks, and even the CEOs of AI companies acknowledge that humans could lose control of the technology. I disagree with the Trump Administration’s hands-off approach. We are being presented with a false choice between “winning the race with China” and protecting the American people. We can and must do both.

AI is unlike electricity or railroads in that it can kill more people, is advancing rapidly, and is being developed entirely by the private sector. We already regulate every industry that can cause harm, like airplanes and drugs. AI should be no different.

I signed a letter asking Speaker Johnson to keep Congress in session until AI regulations are written. I have also signed onto two bills aimed at requiring a kill switch and the FRONTIER Act, which will require third party auditors. I also support a Select Committee on AI that would address safety, minimize job losses, and make sure Americans have the skills and safety net for this transition.
Sixth is artificial intelligence, where we need independent inspectors and a Select Committee on AI.

The House should also push for a standing AI dialogue with China, so safety incidents can be shared quickly and trust built over time. America can compete with China and protect people at the same time.

I recently got to meet with Arnav Shenoy, a senior at William Fremd High School and the winner of the 2025 Congressional App Challenge in Illinois’s Fifth District! Arnav's app, Oculare AI, is an AI-powered mobile platform developed to address an accessibility crisis in eye disease screening.

Congrats, Arnav!
